title: Tweed: finished only after the loom
notes: Woche 1 im Format Kreidestrich (K1), Reihe Unter dem Fadenzähler, Kalenderthema menswear-20261114-3 (Stoffkunde C04), Thema auf Tweed eingegrenzt. Quellen S1, S2 im Originaltext gelesen. Alter Plan bleibt unverändert.

layout.description: A tweed is not finished when it comes off the loom: it is scoured, milled, given some felting, dried and cropped. Why wool felts: its fibres carry scales. Illustration, sources: Harris Tweed Authority (The Process), Woolmark, Introduction to Wovenwear.
layout.companion_text: Suitwerk shows menswear in detail, drawn rather than claimed. No advertising, no product recommendations.

assets.note: Hintergrund aus dem LAYER des Formats Kreidestrich, keine Clips, keine KI-Bilder.

sources.title: The Woolmark Company: Introduction to Wovenwear (Training Manual), S. 5 (scale structure is the cause of felting; milling is the early stage of felting and an important step for the handle of many woven wool fabrics) and S. 6 (Harris Tweed listed as woollen)

Harris Tweed Authority, The Process

hook_candidates.spoken: What is behind this label on the cloth?
Most people read this number wrong.
The answer is in the thread, not the label.
hook_candidates.on_screen: The answer is in the thread

hook_candidates.spoken: If you only read the label, you miss the cloth.
The same tweed before and after milling.
hook_candidates.visual: Glattes und gewalktes Stoffmuster, der Fadenzähler zeigt die Oberfläche

beats.spoken: On the left, a tweed as it comes off the loom. On the right, the same cloth, finished. It looks different and feels different. In between lie water, soap and a lot of movement.

data.question: The same cloth?
data.source: Harris Tweed Authority, The Process · accessed 02.11.2026

beats.spoken: Take Harris Tweed. According to the Harris Tweed Authority, it is woven on treadle looms at home, not in a mill. After weaving, the cloth is scoured in soapy water and soda. Then it is milled and given a certain amount of felting. Why can wool do that? Its fibres carry fine scales. According to Woolmark, they are the cause of felting.

data.source: Harris Tweed Authority; Woolmark p. 5 · accessed 02.11.2026

beats.spoken: After drying, the cloth is cropped. That removes dead hairs from the surface. Finally, an inspector checks the cloth, and only then does it get the certification mark.

data.source: Harris Tweed Authority, The Process · accessed 02.11.2026

beats.spoken: Remember: tweed is only finished after the loom, scoured, milled and cropped. According to Woolmark, milling is an important step for the handle of many wool fabrics. Next time, run your hand over a tweed. Follow Suitwerk for menswear with an eye for detail.

data.claim: Menswear with an eye for detail.
data.source: Woolmark: Introduction to Wovenwear, p. 5 · accessed 02.11.2026
